case_title: Hakeem Khan & Ors. v. State of M.P.
neutral_facts: The incident occurred on a dark winter evening between two parties involved in a dispute over panchayat elections. The complainant party was attacked by the accused party, resulting in the death of one individual. The trial court found that there were injuries on both sides, with three members of the accused party also sustaining injuries. The trial court noted that identifying seventeen individuals in the dark would be extremely difficult and that the presence of the Sarpanch, a key figure, was questionable. The trial court acquitted all seventeen accused, citing the lack of clear evidence and the possibility of a scuffle without premeditation. The High Court overturned this acquittal, but the Supreme Court ultimately set aside the High Court's judgment, finding that the trial court's reasoning was a possible view on the facts of the case.
